newsitem.title: USA: American Dental sees higher '97 sales.
newsitem.headline: American Dental sees higher '97 sales.

text.p: American Dental Technologies Inc, a maker of dental lasers, said it expects 1997 sales to be above the $20.5 million it reported for all of 1996 on a pro-forma basis.
The company reported sales were $5.5 million for the first quarter, up 5 percent over $5.3 million a year ago. Earnings per share rose to $0.12 from $0.10.

Revenues and gross profit increased primarily due to a 186 percent increase in KCP sales volumes in the United States, the firm said. International KCP sales and dental laser sales volumes were down from last year's first quarter due to dealer inventory adjustments.
ADT's KCP product line sprays away decay, usually without a need for anesthesia. The company last year bought Texas Airsonics Inc, a maker of air abrasive products.
"These results reflect the benefits of the merger and our continuing cost containment efforts," said Ben J. Gallant, president and CEO.
